lessons.title: Introduction
teaches: Chess is a game for two players, one playing White and one playing Black.
Each side has one king. Look for the cross on its crown.
Check means the king is attacked.
Checkmate means the king is in check and no legal response can make it safe.
Treat the other player kindly, whether you win or lose.

lessons.title: Master Game
teaches: Develop pieces onto useful squares and coordinate their attacks.
Opening lines can make active pieces stronger than an opponent's undeveloped pieces.
Morphy's sacrifices in this game create forcing moves and a mating attack.
Calculate the opponent's reply before sacrificing material; piece values alone don't determine a move's quality.

puzzles.title: A rook on the loose

exercise.prompt: Find a safe capture with White's rook.

puzzles.context: Black's rook has no protector. Check whether White can take it without being captured in return.
puzzles.explanation: Rook takes d5 wins the unprotected rook. Black has no recapture in this position.

puzzles.title: Two threats, one knight

exercise.prompt: Move the knight to give check and attack the queen.

puzzles.context: Look for an L-shaped move that attacks two targets at once.
puzzles.explanation: Knight to g6 attacks the king on h8 and queen on e5. Black must answer the check, giving White a chance to capture the queen.

puzzles.title: Close the back door

exercise.prompt: Find a rook move that checkmates Black's king.

puzzles.context: Black's pawns block the king's escape squares. Look for a check along the back rank.
puzzles.explanation: Rook to e8 is checkmate. The rook controls the back rank, while Black's pawns block the king's other exits.

puzzles.title: Bring a teammate

exercise.prompt: Move the queen next to Black's king to give checkmate.

puzzles.context: White's king can protect the queen on its mating square.
puzzles.explanation: Queen to g7 is checkmate. White's king protects the queen, which attacks Black's king and controls its remaining escape squares.

puzzles.title: Introduction · 1

exercise.prompt: Can you find the white king? Click it on the board.

puzzles.explanation: The white king is on e1. Look for the little cross on its crown.

puzzles.title: Introduction · 2

exercise.prompt: The king is attacked, and there's no way to make it safe. What do we call that? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: That's checkmate: the king is attacked, and no legal response can make it safe.

puzzles.title: The Battlefield · 1

exercise.prompt: What is the marked square's name? Find its letter and number, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: The square is g2: file g, rank two. Read the letter first, then the number.

puzzles.title: The Battlefield · 2

exercise.prompt: Is the marked line a file, a rank, or a diagonal? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: It's a file, running up and down the board. This one is the d-file.

puzzles.title: The Pawn · 1

exercise.prompt: This pawn hasn't moved yet. Select both squares it can move to, then check your answer.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn can move to c3 or c4. Its first move may be one or two squares because both are empty.

puzzles.title: The Pawn · 2

exercise.prompt: Which black pawn can White capture? Select that pawn.

puzzles.explanation: White can capture the pawn on f5, one square diagonally forward. The pawn directly ahead can't be captured.

puzzles.title: Pawn Wars · 1

exercise.prompt: White can capture Black's last pawn. Make that winning move.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn on d5 captures the pawn on e6. Black has no pawns left, so White wins Pawn Wars.

puzzles.title: Pawn Wars · 2

exercise.prompt: Who wins this race? White moves first. Count how many moves each pawn needs, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Black wins this race. Its pawn needs two moves, while White's needs four, even though White moves first.

puzzles.title: The Rook · 1

exercise.prompt: Select all the black pawns this rook can capture, then check your answer.

puzzles.explanation: The rook can capture on a6 along its file and on e2 along its rank. It can't capture diagonally.

puzzles.title: The Rook · 2

exercise.prompt: Which pieces can this rook capture now? Select them, or choose No squares if none can be captured.

puzzles.explanation: There are no captures here. The rook's own pawn blocks its line to the black pawn.

puzzles.title: Rampant Rooks · 1

exercise.prompt: In Pawn Hunt, which pawns can this rook capture? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The rook on a1 can capture on a5 or f1 along clear straight lines. The diagonal pawn is out of reach.

puzzles.title: Rampant Rooks · 2

exercise.prompt: In Rooks and Pawns, can Black capture the pawn that just reached the end? Select any available capture, or choose No squares.

puzzles.explanation: There is no capture of the pawn in one rook move. The pawn survives at the far end, so White wins this game.

puzzles.title: The Bishop · 1

exercise.prompt: Which pawn can this bishop capture? Select it on the board.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop can capture on b5 along its diagonal. It can't capture straight ahead.

puzzles.title: The Bishop · 2

exercise.prompt: Could this bishop ever capture the pawn if it stays on that light square? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. The bishop stays on dark squares, so it can't reach that pawn while the pawn stays on a light square.

puzzles.title: Busy Bishops · 1

exercise.prompt: Which black pawns can White's bishops capture now? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on c1 can capture the pawn on e3 along its diagonal.

puzzles.title: Busy Bishops · 2

exercise.prompt: Which pawns can this bishop capture? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on d2 can capture the pawns on a5 and g5. Both are on clear diagonals.

puzzles.title: The Queen · 1

exercise.prompt: Which black piece is safe from this queen? Select that piece.

puzzles.explanation: The knight on e5 is safe from this queen. They don't share a file, rank, or diagonal.

puzzles.title: The Queen · 2

exercise.prompt: Which pieces can the queen capture now? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The queen can capture the bishop on h8. Its own pawn blocks the line to the rook.

puzzles.title: Quirky Queens · 1

exercise.prompt: One of these captures loses the queen. Make the capture that keeps it safe.

puzzles.explanation: Queen to g6 is the safe capture here. Capturing on b4 would let the pawn on a3 capture the queen in reply.

puzzles.title: Quirky Queens · 2

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Which pawns can the queen capture now? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The queen can capture the pawn on h7 along its diagonal, stopping that pawn from reaching the end.

puzzles.title: The Knight · 1

exercise.prompt: Which white pieces can this black knight capture? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The knight can capture the rooks on d6 and g5. Both are an L-shaped move from e4.

puzzles.title: The Knight · 2

exercise.prompt: Select all the squares this knight can move to from the corner.

puzzles.explanation: From a1, the knight can move to b3 or c2. Each destination is an L-shaped move away.

puzzles.title: Hungry Horses · 1

exercise.prompt: White moves first. Select all the pieces its knight can capture now.

puzzles.explanation: The knight on e8 can capture the pawns on c7 and g7. Both are legal L-shaped destinations in this challenge.

puzzles.title: Hungry Horses · 2

exercise.prompt: Which two squares does this black pawn attack? Select both.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn attacks b5 and d5, the two squares diagonally forward from c6.

puzzles.title: The King · 1

exercise.prompt: Select every square where this king can move safely.

puzzles.explanation: The king can move safely to c3. The other neighbouring destinations are attacked or unavailable.

puzzles.title: The King · 2

exercise.prompt: Which squares can this king move to safely? Select all of them.

puzzles.explanation: The king can move safely to d1 or f1. The rook attacks the neighbouring squares on the rank above.

puzzles.title: The King · 3

exercise.prompt: Can White's king move to the marked square beside Black's king? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. Moving to e5 would put the kings on neighbouring squares, which isn't allowed.

puzzles.title: Mine Alert · 1

exercise.prompt: The rook attacks this row. May the king move onto the marked square? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. The rook attacks e5, so that square isn't a safe destination for the king.

puzzles.title: Mine Alert · 2

exercise.prompt: Move the king towards e8, choosing one safe neighbouring square at a time.

puzzles.explanation: The route reaches e8 using safe neighbouring squares. In this challenge, avoid the black pieces and every square they attack.

puzzles.title: Check and Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: Can Black's king capture anything safely here? Select any available captures, or choose No squares.

puzzles.explanation: The king has no safe capture here. The checking pawn is protected by another pawn.

puzzles.title: Check and Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: Which three responses can get a king out of check? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Avoid, block, capture: move the king to safety, block the attacker's line, or capture the checking piece with a legal move.

puzzles.title: Check and Checkmate · 3

exercise.prompt: Look at this position. Is Black in check, checkmate, or stalemate? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: It's check, not checkmate. The queen is unprotected here, so the king can capture it and get out of check.

puzzles.title: Getting Your King Safe · 1

exercise.prompt: Select the square where White's king will land after castling.

puzzles.explanation: The king lands on g1, two squares towards the kingside rook. The rook then moves to f1.

puzzles.title: Getting Your King Safe · 2

exercise.prompt: Can White castle kingside in this position? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. The knight is between the king and rook. That path must be clear before White can castle.

puzzles.title: Setting Up the Board Correctly · 1

exercise.prompt: Where does White's queen start? Select its square.

puzzles.explanation: White's queen starts on d1, a light square. Remember: the queen starts on its own colour.

puzzles.title: Setting Up the Board Correctly · 2

exercise.prompt: Which reminder helps you face the board correctly? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Light on the right. The nearest right-hand corner should be light when you face the board.

puzzles.title: Why We Should Castle · 1

exercise.prompt: Which king is safer in this position? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: White's king is safer in this position. It has castled behind its pawns, away from the central action.

puzzles.title: Why We Should Castle · 2

exercise.prompt: How many pawns form White's king shelter? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Three pawns form the shelter in front of White's king.

puzzles.title: When You Can or Can't Castle · 1
puzzles.topic: When You Can or Can't Castle

exercise.prompt: Can White castle kingside here? Look at the bishop's diagonal, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. The bishop attacks the square the king would cross. You can't castle through check.

puzzles.title: When You Can or Can't Castle · 2
puzzles.topic: When You Can or Can't Castle

exercise.prompt: Can White castle kingside in this position? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Yes. The king and rook are unmoved, the path is clear, and the king's starting, crossing, and landing squares are safe.

puzzles.title: Pawn Magic · 1

exercise.prompt: Select the pawn that is one move away from promotion.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn on b7 is one square from the last rank. Reaching that rank requires promotion.

puzzles.title: Scoring Points · 1

exercise.prompt: You captured a queen; your friend captured a knight and a pawn. Who captured more material? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: You captured more material. The queen is worth about nine points; a knight and pawn add up to about four.

puzzles.title: Scoring Points · 2

exercise.prompt: Which group has the greater usual value: a rook, or a knight and two pawns? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: The groups have the same usual value: a rook is five, and a knight plus two pawns is three plus one plus one.

puzzles.title: Playtime · 1

exercise.prompt: Select the piece usually worth five points.

puzzles.explanation: The rook on f4 is the piece usually worth five points.

puzzles.title: Playtime · 2

exercise.prompt: Select the piece that can jump over others in an ordinary move.

puzzles.explanation: The knight on b4 can jump over pieces in an ordinary move. A rook crosses the king only during castling.

puzzles.title: Chess Etiquette · 1

exercise.prompt: At a real board, you deliberately touched a knight that can move. What must you do? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Move the knight. At a real board using touch-move, deliberately touching a piece with a legal move commits you to moving it.

puzzles.title: Chess Etiquette · 2

exercise.prompt: You've lost an over-the-board game. Which response shows good sportsmanship? Choose an answer.
exercise.answer: Shake hands and say well done
choices: Shake hands and say well done

puzzles.explanation: A handshake and a kind comment show respect after the game, whether you won or lost.

puzzles.title: Ways to Draw · 1

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Is this checkmate or stalemate? Check whether the king is attacked and whether Black has any legal move.

puzzles.explanation: It's stalemate. Black's king isn't in check, but Black has no legal move, so the game is a draw.

puzzles.title: Ways to Draw · 2

exercise.prompt: Can either player win when only the two kings remain? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. Two kings alone can never checkmate each other, so the game is drawn.

puzzles.title: Chess Tournaments · 1

exercise.prompt: White can checkmate in one move here. Make that move.

puzzles.explanation: Rook to a8 is checkmate. The rook attacks the king along the back rank, and Black has no legal escape, block, or capture.

puzzles.title: Chess Tournaments · 2

exercise.prompt: You deliberately picked up a knight that has a legal move. What must you do? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Move the knight. Deliberately picking it up in a touch-move game requires a legal knight move.

puzzles.title: Chess Language · 1

exercise.prompt: Which square is Black's queen on? Choose its name.

puzzles.explanation: The queen is on g6: file g, rank six.

puzzles.title: Chess Language · 2

exercise.prompt: Which notation names this bishop and its square? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Bc4 names a bishop on c4. B is the bishop's letter; c4 is its square.

puzzles.title: Getting Off to a Good Start · 1
puzzles.topic: Getting Off to a Good Start

exercise.prompt: Move this knight towards the centre rather than the edge.

puzzles.explanation: Knight to f3 develops towards the centre. Here, it has more useful options than on the edge.

puzzles.title: Getting Off to a Good Start · 2
puzzles.topic: Getting Off to a Good Start

exercise.prompt: Make a first pawn move that occupies one of the four central squares.

puzzles.explanation: Both e2 to e4 and d2 to d4 occupy a central square. Either is an accepted opening move in this exercise.

puzzles.title: Chess Maths · 1

exercise.prompt: Should the queen capture this pawn? Consider the other black pawn's reply, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. Taking that pawn lets the other pawn capture the queen, losing about nine points to gain one.

puzzles.title: Chess Maths · 2

exercise.prompt: Who has the greater usual material value here? Don't count the kings. Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: White has ten points of material: queen nine plus pawn one. Black has eight: rook five plus bishop three.

puzzles.title: The Classic Trick · 1

exercise.prompt: Move a pawn to block the queen's path and stop the immediate threat.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn moves from g7 to g6, blocking the queen's line to f7 and attacking the queen.

puzzles.title: The Classic Trick · 2

exercise.prompt: Should Black advance the marked pawn to attack the queen here? Check the unprotected central pawn, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. The pawn push would allow the queen to capture the unprotected central pawn with check and attack the corner rook.

puzzles.title: The Fork · 1

exercise.prompt: Move White's knight to give check and attack the rook at the same time.

puzzles.explanation: Knight to c7 gives check and attacks the rook at the same time. In this position, White wins the rook after Black answers check.

puzzles.title: The Fork · 2

exercise.prompt: Make a pawn move that attacks both the knight and rook.

puzzles.explanation: Pawn to d5 attacks the knight and rook diagonally. That's a pawn fork.

puzzles.title: The Pin · 1

exercise.prompt: Which black piece is pinned? Select it on the board.

puzzles.explanation: The knight on c6 is pinned to its king along the bishop's diagonal. Moving off that line would expose check.

puzzles.title: The Pin · 2

exercise.prompt: This bishop is pinned to the queen, not the king. Is it legally allowed to move? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: Yes. The bishop is pinned to the queen, not the king. Moving may be costly, but it isn't forbidden by king safety here.

puzzles.title: The Skewer · 1

exercise.prompt: Move White's rook to give check along the line with Black's queen behind the king.

puzzles.explanation: Rook to b1 gives check with Black's queen behind the king. When the king leaves the file, the queen becomes exposed.

puzzles.title: The Skewer · 2

exercise.prompt: Is the marked attack a pin or a skewer? Look at which piece is in front, then choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: It's a skewer. The queen is attacked in front of the rook; moving it exposes the rook behind.

puzzles.title: The Discovered Attack or Check · 1

exercise.prompt: Move the knight to capture the queen and open the bishop's line to the king.

puzzles.explanation: The knight captures the queen on c6 and opens the bishop's diagonal, giving discovered check at the same time.

puzzles.title: The Discovered Attack or Check · 2

exercise.prompt: Which white piece blocks the rook's line to Black's king? Select that piece.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on c8 blocks the rook's line. Moving it away uncovers the rook's check.

puzzles.title: Removing the Defender · 1

exercise.prompt: Which black piece protects the knight White wants to capture? Select that piece.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop on c8 protects the knight on a6 along its diagonal.

puzzles.title: Removing the Defender · 2

exercise.prompt: Make a move that captures the bishop defending the knight.

puzzles.explanation: The queen captures the bishop on c8 with check. After Black responds, the rook can capture the knight that bishop was protecting.

puzzles.title: Walking the Dog · 1

exercise.prompt: Make the rook move that gives checkmate.

puzzles.explanation: Rook to a8 checks along the top rank. The other rook cuts off the rank below, leaving the king no escape. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Walking the Dog · 2

exercise.prompt: Keep the fence rook in place. Move the other rook up to give check.

puzzles.explanation: Rook to h6 gives check while the rook on a5 keeps its fence. That forces the king further towards the edge.

puzzles.title: Queen and King Checkmate · 1

exercise.prompt: Should the queen follow again now that the king is in the corner? Choose an answer.

puzzles.explanation: No. Following again would remove the king's last move without giving check. That would be stalemate, a draw.

puzzles.title: Queen and King Checkmate · 2

exercise.prompt: Find a queen move that checkmates Black's king in one move.

puzzles.explanation: Queen to b7 or a7 mates close to the king. Queen to c8, d8, or e8 mates along the top rank. Each gives check with no legal escape.

puzzles.title: Box Them In · 1

exercise.prompt: Find the rook move that gives checkmate.

puzzles.explanation: Rook to f8 gives check along the top rank. White's king controls the escape squares, so it's checkmate.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 1: Winning Material · 1

exercise.prompt: First, capture the knight that protects the bishop. Make that move on the board.

puzzles.explanation: The bishop captures the knight on f6 with check. After the king recaptures, the rook can take the bishop on d5, which has lost its defender.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 1: Winning Material · 2

exercise.prompt: Move the bishop to pin Black's queen to its king.

puzzles.explanation: Bishop to b2 pins the queen to the king. Here, the queen can't escape along the diagonal without losing material.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 1: Winning Material · 3

exercise.prompt: Advance the pawn to attack both black rooks at once.

puzzles.explanation: Pawn to c4 forks the rooks on b5 and d5. In this position, Black can't save both, and one rook is also pinned.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 1: Winning Material · 4

exercise.prompt: Make a knight move that gives check and helps win Black's unprotected queen.

puzzles.explanation: Knight to f6 or g5 gives check and opens the queen's diagonal towards d5. In the demonstrated reply, Black captures the knight and White captures the queen.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 2: Mate in One · 1

exercise.prompt: Find a move that checkmates Black's king. There may be more than one solution.

puzzles.explanation: Queen to f8 is mate, with the pawn protecting the queen. Rook to d8 also mates: the queen and pawn cover g7, and Black can't block or capture the rook.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 2: Mate in One · 2

exercise.prompt: Find a bishop move that checkmates Black's king.

puzzles.explanation: Bishop to a5 gives check. The bishop controls the open escape squares, and Black's own pieces block the others. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 2: Mate in One · 3

exercise.prompt: Move the rook to uncover checkmate from the bishop.

puzzles.explanation: The rook captures on g4, opening the bishop's check and controlling the king's escape line. Black has no legal response. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Puzzle Section 2: Mate in One · 4

exercise.prompt: Find a pawn capture that gives checkmate in this position.

puzzles.explanation: The pawn captures on f7, checking the king and uncovering check from the rook. No legal king move answers both attacks. Checkmate.

puzzles.title: Master Game · 1

exercise.prompt: Move White's queen to the top rank to give check and set up a forced mate.

puzzles.explanation: Queen to b8 gives check and forces the knight to capture it. White then plays rook to d8, protected by the bishop, giving checkmate.
